_comment: Mutation testing breaks the code on purpose and checks whether a test goes red.
A passing suite cannot see a test named for a behaviour whose body does not exercise it, a
double that cannot represent the failing state, or a guard nobody has watched fail. A green
count says the tests ran, not that they would notice.
Scoped to src/wallet, the logic that decides money (amounts, purchases, addresses, the
domain lifecycle). Screens are driven by their own flow tests and mutate poorly, since most
changes there produce a render nobody asserted on rather than a wrong answer.
A threshold belongs at what the suite reaches, not at an aspiration, because a threshold
nobody can meet is ignored. break stays null, so the score is reported and never fails a run.
ignorePatterns keeps the sandbox to what the tests read. Copying the repository whole fails
outright on the symlinks inside ios/Pods, and copying android and ios build output costs
minutes per run for directories no test opens.
enableFindRelatedTests runs each mutant against only the suites that import the file it
touched. Without it every mutant reruns the whole suite, which takes hours for a single file.
The screen flow tests are excluded from the run instead, since they time out under the sandbox
and would not judge a wrong amount anyway.
